claim_scope.narrowed: fixed-session packets remain a strong low-work drilldown baseline, and some tasks need better ranking policies or analyst studies
claim_scope.not_supported: human accuracy/time improvement, automatic detection, universal dominance over fixed-session baselines, or complete trace-ecosystem compatibility
claim_scope.supported: operation stacks provide a configurable, two-abstraction way to inspect real labeled failure, safety, quality, and boundary tasks without collapsing to flat traces or hard-coding session boundaries

headline: R309 synthesizes existing labeled-task evidence into reviewer-facing problem cards across 4 datasets, 6 tasks, and 34539 task-operations. Operation stacks are more selective than flat packets on all 6 tasks, contain high-lift evidence in 5/6 tasks, and have higher selected recall than fixed-session packets on 5/6 tasks. Fixed sessions remain cheaper on selected work in 4/6 tasks, so the paper claim remains an inspectability tradeoff rather than universal dominance.
input_policy: no dataset sync; reads tracked R298/R300/R302/R305/R308 artifacts only

novelty_claims.evidence: C1 supported by 15 public labeled sources plus local trace exchange.
novelty_claims.why_new: The profiler does not privilege prompt, session, span, GUI, safety, or quality objects; they are operation shapes or fields.

novelty_claims.evidence: R286 depth sweep and R293 profile-spec override on identical operations.
novelty_claims.why_new: Folded-stack output is reused, but frames come from semantic operation fields and can be changed after capture.

novelty_claims.evidence: R282/R285 mapping generalization and R297 learned boundary backend.
novelty_claims.why_new: Regex mappings, learned label-derived mappings, and supervised boundary backends all write operation fields before folding.

novelty_claims.claim: Non-flamegraph diagnostic views over real labels
novelty_claims.evidence: R288/R289/R290/R291 diagnostics and R296 evidence packet.
novelty_claims.why_new: Quality, looping, safety, attack, redundancy, and human-group labels become stackable and scoreable fields.

novelty_context.paper_ready_takeaway: AgentSight should claim configurable semantic profiling over real labeled agent trajectories: operations provide the common record, operation stacks provide recursive query-time folding, and mappings/boundary backends only derive fields before folding. The evidence supports mechanism and diagnostic value, not unsupervised intent discovery or developer productivity.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: 15 datasets, 47590 operations, 1611 stacks in the supplemental smoke set.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: Does not prove full-scale conversion of every public benchmark or image/video archive.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: The paper artifact under test is a two-object profiler model, not another fixed agent trace viewer.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Normalize every source row into operations, then use operation stacks as query-time projections.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: 15 public labeled trajectory sources with dataset/session/task/action/quality fields.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: Agent traces mix prompts, tools, GUI actions, API calls, safety labels, and quality labels; prompt/session/span object models split these into incompatible pipelines.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: R286 folds the same 13265 operations from 9 dataset stacks to 57 phase, 455 action, and 3757 fixed-session stacks; R293 stack override reduces AgentNet stacks by 86.349%.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: Does not identify one universal best stack for every task.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: Recursive folding is a query over operation fields rather than a hard-coded prompt/session hierarchy.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Fold the same operations at different stack depths by changing only the stack specification.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: R286 depth sweep and R293 AgentNet profile-spec override.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: The useful boundary depends on the debugging question; a fixed session/prompt stack either hides phase structure or fragments aggregation.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: R282 mapping reduces held-out unique stacks by 26.408% and improves compression by 35.889%; R285 has 0 negative folds; R297 supervised boundary F1 is 0.7735.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: Does not support unsupervised or cross-family general boundary detection.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: Mapping/tagging and boundary backends are one extension point: derive fields, never introduce a third profiler object.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Run deterministic or learned field derivation before stack construction, then fold ordinary operation fields.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: R282 held-out mappings, R285 leave-dataset-out mappings, and R297 held-out OSWorld-Human boundary labels.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: Raw dataset labels and action names are inconsistent; without field derivation, stacks are either too shallow or too fragmented.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: Conservative human-group projection reaches boundary F1 0.6268 at precision 1.0; R297 learned backend improves over phase/action/target baselines and folds 1132 held-out operations into 74 stacks.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: R290 conservative recall is limited; R297 is supervised and OSWorld-only.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: The same action sequence supports action-depth, human-group-depth, and learned-boundary-depth views.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Carry human-group labels and learned-group fields as stackable operation fields.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: OSWorld-Human single-action and grouped-action human trajectories.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: Desktop agents often need subtask-level inspection below a task but above a raw click/key action.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: AgentRewardBench repeat-signal/looping V-measure is 0.3777 versus 0.0105 for step-error; SATraj has 622 unsafe operations; AgentNet step_correct and step_redundant fields have 16741 and 16741 covered operations.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: Does not prove developer productivity or automatic quality prediction.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: The profiler exposes non-flamegraph quality and safety views without creating separate failure or safety profilers.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Represent expert labels, safety labels, and sequence-derived repetition signals as operation fields, then score and visualize them with stack reports.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: AgentRewardBench expert looping labels, SATraj-OS safety labels, and AgentNet step correctness/redundancy labels.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: Agent debugging requires failure, safety, looping, and step-quality diagnostics, not only hot paths.

real_problem_blocks.headline_evidence: R294 trace import and operation import folded outputs are identical; R296 indexes 11 visualization/evidence entries and 4 reviewer questions.
real_problem_blocks.limitations: Reviewer packets are synthesis artifacts, not new empirical evidence.
real_problem_blocks.novelty_value: The contribution includes an auditable research workflow around configurable profiler queries, not just a rendered flamegraph.
real_problem_blocks.profiler_mechanism: Use tracked profile specs, trace exchange, claim synthesis, and reviewer evidence packets as reproducibility surfaces.
real_problem_blocks.public_oracle: R293 profile spec, R294 trace exchange, R295 claim synthesis, and R296 reviewer packet.
real_problem_blocks.real_problem: Paper claims drift when results are scattered across shell commands, folded files, and one-off visualizations.
